newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Renault says Belgian PM knew of closure plans.
newsitem.headline: Renault says Belgian PM knew of closure plans.

text.p: Top Belgian politicians knew in advance of the planned closure of a French-owned car factory which sparked angry protests when it was announced three months ago, Renault president Louis Schweitzer told a Belgian newspaper on Saturday.

Schweitzer said in an interview with French language newspaper "L'Echo" that Prime Minister Jean Luc Dehaene and President of the Flanders regional government Luc Van den Brande had pushed for early release of the news on February 27 that the Vilvoorde Renault plan would close.

"I have the feeling that... the politicians concerned and the Belgian unions never held any illusions. Those concerned politically -- Jean Luc Dehaene and Luc Van den Brande -- were informed in advance and they themselves wanted us to make our decision public quickly," Schweitzer.
Renault's closure plans for the plant, which employs 3,100 staff, sparked angry protest strikes and demonstrations by Belgian car workers.

Schweitzer said he would respect Belgian and French court rulings criticising the lack of consultation ahead of the closure annoiuncement and requiring the company to meet representatives of its European staff on June 3 to discuss the shutdown.
The judgments do not, however, bear on the closure decision itself.

Renault has said it needs to close the plant as part of a plan to streamline its money-losing European operations. Vilvoorde is not the mother plant for any new models and its production can easily be shifted to other plants, it says.
Renault initially said the plant was to be closed by the end of July but has since said the deadline could be extended by a few weeks or months.
